newsitem.title: USA: Fed's Philllips urges more disclosure by big banks.
newsitem.headline: Fed's Philllips urges more disclosure by big banks.

text.p: The biggest banks and other financial institutions must disclose more fully the risks they take if they expect a lighter regulatory burden, Federal reserve Governor Susan Phillips said on Friday.

"We applaud recent efforts on the part of some managements to increase voluntary risk disclosures in footnotes to their financial statements, but still more can and should be done," Phillips said in prepared remarks for delivery to the Atlanta Society of Financial Analysts in Atlanta, Ga.
A text was issued in advance in Washington.

Phillips emphasized "the chances of a repeat of the banking crisis of the late 1980s have been reduced," but said market efficiency would benefit if stock analysts and bond rating agencies knew more about the risks that banks take.
She said that while bank examiners "have access to the most intimate details of a bank's business," there was a growing need for a broader awareness of this information.

"This need has become especially evident as market participants and others call for expanded powers and/or reduced regulatory burdens based on so-called market tests of 'good management' or 'adequate capital'," Phillips said.

Phillips said that as a bank regulator, "I would not want to rely even partially on the market's assessment of the capital adequacy of a bank -- unless I were assured theat market analysts had the data to reach informed conclusions."
In general, Phillips said, while banks engage in more complex risk-taking now than they used to do, they also have stronger capital levels than they did in the 1980s.
In addition, she added, banks measure risks better and have more sophisticated management controls in place so that the safety and soundness of the banking system has been enhanced.
